cohort: The study included 498 mother-baby dyads observed during childbirth care in three public hospitals in Addis Ababa.
finding: All observed newborns (100%) experienced at least one form of disrespect and abuse (D&A), with physical abuse being common, and various factors including preterm birth, female sex, maternal rural residence, unmarried maternal status, fewer ANC visits, and instrument-assisted delivery were significantly associated with higher D&A.
mod_finding: Newborns delivered assisted by instrument had a higher likelihood of experiencing D&A (AOR = 2.19; 95%CI: 1.20-3.99).
cross-section timing: From the first stage of labor through two hours after birth
gest_age: Gestational age at birth was a measured variable, with preterm newborns having a higher likelihood of D&A.
